facts.text: Turtle Lake’s name comes from the Salish word čɫqq̓liʔ, meaning 'turtle,' a symbol of longevity and protection in local tribal lore.
The 49‑acre reservoir, created by the 1931‑32 Turtle Lake Dam, holds 899 acre‑feet of water for the Flathead Irrigation Project.
At 3,097 feet elevation, the lake supports a Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks fishery that stocks native westslope cutthroat trout.
Seasonal wetlands around Turtle Lake create diverse habitats, boosting local biodiversity with aquatic and avian species across the Flathead Valley.
Average temperatures swing from 18°F in January to 84°F in July, with nearby Flathead Lake moderating extremes.
Lewis and Clark’s 1805‑06 passage through Salish lands introduced trade goods that subtly reshaped tribal migration patterns.
